content.text:
## The Heart of the Rose (Fractal Mural)

**Also Known As**:

*   _Crimson Passion_
*   _El Pulpo Hipnotico_
*   _The Crimson Ratio_

The "Heart of the Rose" is one of my oldest, most well-known, and also most stolen designs across the entire internet. As of 2016, now that it's a mural at the Sofitel SO Hua Hin Resort & Spa, it may as well be in the public domain. It's an achievement that none can take from me -- my first mural _ever_.

At 16 by 10 feet (or 5x3 meters for you metric folks), this beast is my absolute largest mural to date. The design was contracted by [Atelier Donatien Carratier](https://atelierdonatiencarratier.com/) for the [SO Hua Hin resort and spa](https://www.so-sofitel-huahin.com/) out in Thailand. I built "The Heart of the Rose" from the ground up in Ultra Fractal, dialing in the exact specs, depth, and colors they were hunting for. We rendered the final cut onto professional 3M tiles and slapped it directly onto the resort's corridor wall.

She finally saw the light of day on February 19, 2016.

She goes by a few names out in the wild: _Heart of the Rose_, _Crimson Passion_, _The Crimson Ratio_, and my personal favorite... _El Pulpo Hipnotico_. Prints, pillows, and more are available [here on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/20966118). Note that while you'll find her for sale in other places, Redbubble or myself are your only trusted sources. If you'd like her on a specific product that you don't see, [contact me](contact). I own the original weights and equation, therefore making it easy to apply the rose to nearly any design.

content.caption: Original design specification for _"The Heart of the Rose"_

texts:
## ACCOR's Sofitel SO Hua Hin Resort & Spa

The resort itself was birthed by the famed Thai architect Duangrit "Duang" Bunnag. The man has this incredibly natural, artistic way of forging buildings that don't just sit on the land -- they work _with_ it. To me, his architecture feels like a modern take on ancient shrines; you can physically feel the heavy spiritual weight behind his intentions. SO Hua Hin is no exception.

Here’s the hilarious irony of it all: despite how many times that original render got ripped off and stolen over the years, it was actually one of those bootlegged copies that led Donatien Carratier straight to my doorstep. He came asking if I could re-render the design for a massive mural with updated specs. When he finally dropped the actual scale on me, I straight-up told him I wasn't even sure my rig could render something _that_ monstrous. He gave me exactly three days to figure it out. Somewhere in that seventy-two-hour window, I hacked together a technique that actually let me pull it off.

Art isn't just an afterthought at SO Hua Hin -- it's the absolute lifeblood. From the heavily stylized grounds to the classical pieces holding down one wing, to the abstract and surreal chaos dominating the other... there sits my fractal mural, dead center, acting as the bridge that connects the madness. Even the rooms have been dialed in by absolute masters of the craft.

When the resort bagged the World Luxury Spa Award back in 2021, I like to think my mural played at least some small part in securing that crown. It was my very first large-scale installation. And while I've thrown up other massive murals since then, like my now-famous "[Celestial Return](celestial-return)" . . absolutely none of them have ever matched the sheer, crushing immensity of the _Heart of the Rose_ herself.

content.text:
## The Crimson Ratio: Prehistory

When you get right down to the bones of it, there are two distinct generations of this design: the era _before_ SO Hua Hin, and the era _after_. That original pre-resort render? It was honestly a bit fuzzy even at 1080p, rocking a lot more pinks, violets, and lavenders bleeding out into those outstretched spirals. But for the massive mural cut, the powers that be requested I take the knotting points -- right where the spirals violently crash together -- and drown them in shadow until they were practically undecipherable. The differences end right there.

The real magic hiding in both cuts comes down to the lighting. I rigged the scene with a dual-light setup (one stark white, one pure crimson) fighting against a dual-shadow rig (one pitch black, one burning orange). But the absolute secret sauce is baked right into the texture itself. It acts like a sponge, soaking up those conflicting light and shadow sources and dragging them down through the spiral -- magnifying the intensity with every single level... descending into absolute madness. You can see how I've applied a similar technique to a few [other mandelbrots](other-mandelbrot-fractals).

I actually weaponized a similar, albeit far more subtle, version of this exact technique in my crowd-favorite "[Mother of Pearl](mother-of-pearl)" piece, as well as the deeper-cut "Lavender Mandelbrot."

Outside of So Hua Hin, you can find the original post from me on Instagram ([link](https://www.instagram.com/p/BEeZrj4Nqka/)) and merchandise on Redbubble ([link](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/20966118)).

Rendered in Ultra Fractal 5. Designed by San Jaya Prime (aka, "Kan Men Caban Ix Lamat").

## Extended Exploration

For those who like this one, but would seek a finer, more subtle piece, then "[Mother of Pearl](mother-of-pearl)" may be exactly the treasure you seek. The "Heart of the Rose" appears as a full-page borderless feature in my "[Spectral Iteration](spectral-iteration)" book, along with my "[Nocturne of Scorpio](nocturne-of-scorpio)" fractal painting.
